bluetooth_confirm.title: Add {name}
bluetooth_confirm.description:
Set up {name}?

After you add it, Home Assistant will ask you to put the shower into pairing mode to establish its Bluetooth bond.

pair_confirm.title: Pair {name}
pair_confirm.description:
The shower's Bluetooth security bond needs (re)establishing — this can only be done from the unit itself.

**Before you press Submit:**

1. Go to the shower and put it into **pairing / Bluetooth mode** at the panel (or power-cycle the unit so it is freshly pairable).
2. **Only once it is pairable**, press **Submit** below.

Home Assistant will then bond and verify over the proxy (about 10–30s). If it fails, put the unit back into pairing mode and Submit again.

Last attempt: {detail}

error.pair_failed: Pairing did not complete — make sure the shower is in pairing mode and in range, then Submit again. Detail: {detail}

abort.entry_not_found: Could not find the device entry to re-pair.
abort.pair_successful: Paired and verified — the shower is bonded and ready. {detail}

bond_lost.title: {name} needs re-pairing
bond_lost.description:
The Bluetooth security bond to {name} was lost, so the shower can't be controlled.

To fix it: put the shower into pairing mode at the panel, then go to Settings → Devices & Services → Mira Activate → the device's ⋮ menu → **Reconfigure**, and follow the on-screen steps.

proxy_wedged.title: {name}: BLE proxy appears wedged — restart the proxy
proxy_wedged.description:
The security bond to {name} has been failing for over an hour even though the shower is still advertising and connectable. This pattern means the ESPHome BLE proxy's Bluetooth stack is wedged (commonly after a crash/panic reboot) — the bond itself is almost certainly intact.

**Do NOT re-pair.** Restart the BLE proxy instead (its Restart button in Home Assistant, or power-cycle it). The shower should recover within a few minutes of the proxy coming back.
